newsitem.title: USA: Foreign crudes to U.S. quieted by narrow arbitrage.
newsitem.headline: Foreign crudes to U.S. quieted by narrow arbitrage.

text.p: Foreign crude trade to the U.S. was again quiet on Wednesday, depressed by the lack of economic incentive to bring barrels from overseas.
U.S. refiners are finding it difficult to accomodate imports of foreign crude due to weak margins and cheaper domestic parcels available.
Crude brokers said the arbitrage windows for various crudes, notably Brent, remained too narrow for attracting deals.
Dated Brent deals sold in London were done at slightly cheaper levels, as lack of demand saw the latest deal for an Oct 1-3 date sold at November paper +6 cents.
